newsitem.title: USA: HOLOCAUST PLAINTIFFS DEMAND ACCESS TO GERMAN FILES.
newsitem.headline: HOLOCAUST PLAINTIFFS DEMAND ACCESS TO GERMAN FILES.

text.p: Attorneys for Holocaust victims and their families said they are demanding that the German government grant them the same access to privileged files that has been given to German insurer Allianz AG Holding and its affiliates.

New York law firm Anderson Kill & Olick, which is representing the plaintiffs, said it has learned that the German Restitution Office has granted Allianz special government permission to research the privileged and confidential files related to Holocaust victims.
However, the plaintiffs' request for similar access has been denied by the German government, Anderson Kill said in a statement.
Allianz is one of 16 insurers named in a complaint filed earlier this year by Holocaust victims and their families.
The suit claims that insurance policies held by the victims and their families, were confiscated by the Nazis and then improperly transferred, liquidated or cashed in.
Anderson Kill plans to hold a news conference on the matter on Thursday morning.
In the statement, Anderson Kill said the government waived the normal requirements that a notarized original power of attorney and inheritance papers be provided.

Michael Witti, the plaintiffs' German co-counsel in the class action was told that Allianz claimed "justified legal interest" in obtaining access to Holocaust victims' confidential and privileged documents, Anderson Kill said.

Witti's request to review the same files has been denied unless the plaintiffs present original power of attorney and inheritance papers -- the condition waived for the Allianz defendants, the law firm said.
